audit.whatIsWrong: The page says Blinding Assault negates 'your Q AA and spin damage' and 'blocks your AAs'.
audit.why: Judgment is not a basic attack — Riot's text is 'Garen rapidly spins his sword around his body, dealing physical damage to nearby enemies'. No blind or vision effect can reduce it. Quinn's Q is described by Riot as marking an enemy and hindering its vision, so at most it costs Garen his Decisive Strike auto and his sight of her; his spin keeps ticking at full damage. The current wording talks a player out of the exact tool that wins him the trade.
audit.corrected: Her Q can blank the Decisive Strike auto and cut your vision; it does nothing to Judgment.

audit.whatIsWrong: Vault's cooldown is stated as 11s, and its interrupt is never mentioned.
audit.why: Riot data: Vault is 12/11/10/9/8s — 11s is Blinding Assault's rank-1 cooldown, so the two spells' timers have been swapped. Vault also 'leaps off the target, briefly interrupting it' and slows, which is what breaks a Garen commit, not the knockback the page describes.
audit.corrected: Vault is 12s at rank 1, and it briefly interrupts you as she leaps off.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers disagree with each other and with the packet: content gives Quinn six of seven stages, the full layer gives her five, and the packet chart gives Garen five. The packet itself flags the contradiction ('Garen wins only 47.24% but the chart gives Garen 5/7 stages').
audit.why: Two authorities point opposite ways here, so no flip can be made safely: the packet levelChart says Garen takes over from level 3, while the win rate (47.24% over 870 games, the only losing matchup in this slice) says Quinn wins the lane overall. The why-text follows the packet chart. Guessing which one to honour would ship a wrong trade calendar either way.
Suffer the ranged early game, take over once you can stick to her, win the sidelane 1v1 against a squishy marksman — the early/mid/late prose is coherent and matches the kits.

edits.before: Track Quinn’s Vault (Dash/Blind) (11s): Her self-peel. Q-close when down. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Vault (12s at rank 1) is her self-peel, and it briefly interrupts you as she leaps off. Close while it is down.

edits.before: Fight into her blind. Poke-war from range. Let her free-farm. And keep the ultimate holstered until a kill is actually on the table.
edits.after: Stop spinning because she blinded you. Poke-war from range. Let her free-farm. And keep the ultimate holstered until a kill is on the table.

edits.before: Track his Quinn Quinn Harrier marks and Vault chest bounce peel before you commit
edits.after: Track her Vault (12s at rank 1) — that leap is what denies your kill window

edits.before: Quinn's early ranged harass is brutal — Blinding Assault (Q) blocks your AAs and Vault (E) knocks you back out of spin range, so levels 1-2 are miserable for you.
edits.after: Quinn's early ranged harass is brutal — Blinding Assault (Q) blanks your Decisive Strike auto and Vault (E) leaps her out of spin range, so levels 1-2 are miserable for you.

edits.before: Use the blind to negate your Q AA and spin damage
edits.after: Use Blinding Assault to blank your Q auto-attack

edits.before: Q-silence and lock her so she can't Vault (E) away
edits.after: Keep spinning through her Q — Judgment ignores the blind

notes: Level chart deliberately NOT edited — see questionsForUser. The packet's own defect list says the chart contradicts the win rate, and the two layers already disagree with each other, so any flip would be a guess about which authority governs. Everything else in the entry was corrected. Not asserted: whether Blinding Assault is a true blind (attack misses) or a nearsight — Riot's text only says it marks an enemy and 'hinder[s] its vision', which does not settle it, so the rewrite claims only that it costs Garen his Decisive Strike auto and that Judgment is unaffected, which holds either way.
